title: Cross-Encoder Reranking: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Funnel Meets Reranker | the recall/precision funnel from the previous lesson with a slider over how many candidates the cross-encoder rescores, pricing each depth at 32 pairs per 18 ms batch | the reranker's cost is linear in candidates and independent of corpus size, so it can never run first — it is what forces the funnel, and 100 candidates is 4 batches, about 60-75 ms

2. Reading Both Together | three queries (jaguar 0-60 time, exercises that do not load the knee, laptop under 4 pounds) rendered as the [CLS] query [SEP] document [SEP] sequence, toggled between joint attention and two independently encoded 768-float vectors | joint query-document attention is what resolves word sense, binds negation to its object and compares 3.8 lb against 4 pounds; nothing about a document can be precomputed, and the output logit is not a calibrated probability

3. Compress Now Or Later | corpus size dragged from 1,000 to 10,000,000 passages, with bi-encoder query cost against full-corpus cross-encoder cost and the effectiveness pill | the bi-encoder compresses a document into 768 floats before the query is known and wins on efficiency; the cross-encoder defers and wins on effectiveness by several nDCG points; one million passages is over nine minutes per query, so they are complements, with a legitimate single-stage exception below a few thousand documents

4. Finding The Knee | the depth sweep (20/50/100/200 at nDCG 0.410-0.455 and p95 25-180 ms) against a draggable tail-latency budget, with a first-stage toggle that moves the candidate ceiling from rank 150 to rank 40 | pick the knee at your tail budget rather than the largest affordable depth, because 200 buys 0.003 nDCG for double the latency; depth below the candidate ceiling means the reranker never sees the relevant document, and depth is a property of the retriever-reranker pair so the sweep is void when either stage changes

5. Depth Is Capacity | query rate and rerank depth sliders producing pairs per second, replicas at 2,500 pairs/sec each, and a traffic-peak toggle showing the shortfall that falls back to retrieval order | 200 qps at depth 100 is 20,000 pairs/sec and eight replicas, halving depth halves the fleet, and the fallback to unreranked retrieval order is the evaluated degraded mode — which is how doubling depth for a small offline gain made production worse
